articles.title: Michael Polansky is training an AI model on skin that’s still alive
articles.summary: Michael Polansky — better known publicly as Lady Gaga's partner and a former top deputy to Sean Parker — has quietly spent years building an AI-driven startup that keeps living human skin tissue alive for weeks outside the body to discover new skincare compounds, and is only now going public about it.

articles.title: Japanese space tech startup Letara expands beyond satellite thrusters with $16M
articles.summary: Japanese space startup Letara is betting its hybrid rocket technology can move beyond small satellite thrusters into a broader market for space, defense and security, after raising ¥2.6 billion ($16 million).

articles.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
articles.summary: Anthropic forbids its Claude models from generating sexually explicit content. But a series of tests conducted by TechCrunch found that it didn't take much to get past the restriction.

articles.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
articles.summary: Nvidia continues to pour money into data center development — just as AI data centers bring lots of money into Nvidia.

articles.title: How AI accounting startup Rillet raised $100M and became a unicorn in 48 hours
articles.summary: Rillet CEO Nicolas Kopp shared growth numbers at a board meeting and set off a fundraising frenzy from Iconiq, Sequoia and others. Without even trying.

articles.title: Apple is reportedly cutting hundreds of jobs from Siri, Vision Pro teams

articles.title: TikTok reaches $400M settlement over children’s privacy lawsuit
articles.summary: Two years after the U.S. Department of Justice alleged that TikTok violated the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act, it has reached a $400 million settlement.

articles.title: The $225 Pebble Time 2 is a refreshingly fun smartwatch
articles.summary: The $225 Pebble Time 2 pairs quirky watch faces and apps with physical buttons, an e-paper display, weeks of battery life, and a playful hacker spirit.

articles.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
articles.summary: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.

articles.title: Last chance: Save up to $300 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket today
articles.summary: If you’ve been circling around Disrupt, then now’s the best time to lock in your pass and start getting ready to join the rest of the startup community gathering in San Francisco from October 13-15 at Moscone West!

articles.summary: The responses to NHTSA's questions so far are redacted entirely, citing "confidential business information."

articles.title: Why is the DOJ investigating Andreessen Horowitz’s board seats?
articles.summary: Andreessen Horowitz has two partners sitting on the boards of companies that now compete with each other: Ben Horowitz at Databricks and Martin Casado at Fivetran. Nothing too scandalous on the surface, except the Department of Justice has reportedly been investigating the arrangement for almost a year, dusting off a 112-year-old antitrust law that’s rarely used against VCs.  Board conflicts aren’t exactly new, and these companies weren’t necessarily direct competitors when a16z first invested […]

articles.title: US government lab is probing Chinese lidar for security vulnerabilities
articles.summary: The security review is being performed by the Idaho National Laboratory, and the research is being funded by a company -- or a group of companies -- in the electric and autonomous vehicle industries.

articles.title: Oura faces lawsuit accusing it of misleading consumers about sleep-tracking accuracy
articles.summary: The lawsuit alleges that Oura rings are unable to measure any of the physiological signals needed to assess sleep quality or determine sleep stages.
